gaps.sentence: ___ of the milk has gone off, so do not drink it.
gaps.explanation: 'All of the milk' — 'whole' would need 'the whole of the milk'.

gaps.sentence: She speaks ___ Spanish and Italian fluently.
gaps.explanation: 'Both ... and ...' links two items affirmatively; 'neither/either' pair with 'nor/or'.

gaps.sentence: There are plenty ___ chairs for everyone.
gaps.hint: 'plenty' is always followed by this preposition before a noun
gaps.explanation: 'Plenty of + noun' is the fixed pattern; no other preposition follows 'plenty'.

gaps.sentence: There are too ___ tourists in Venice in August.
gaps.explanation: 'Too many' is used before countable plurals like tourists; 'too much' is for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my two brothers work in banking.
gaps.explanation: 'Both of my two brothers work ...' is correct; 'all' and 'none' are not used for two.

gaps.sentence: There were ___ interruptions this year, so the ceremony ran far more smoothly.
You can park on ___ side of the street.
gaps.hint: singular noun meaning 'this one or that one'
gaps.explanation: 'Either side' means one side or the other (both are allowed); 'both' would need the plural 'sides'.

gaps.sentence: We see our grandparents ___ other weekend.
gaps.explanation: 'Every other weekend' means alternate weekends; 'each other' has a different, reciprocal meaning.
